species.name: Crappie
why: Water 64°F on top, a bit cool for them, so they feed in the warmest water they can find.
Best water today is 8–30 ft deep, mostly on channel edges.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 50 ft, cold below.

species.name: White bass
why: Water 64°F on top, a bit cool for them, so they feed in the warmest water they can find.
Best water today is 10–30 ft deep, mostly on channel edges.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 50 ft, cold below.

species.name: Walleye
why: Water 64°F on top, a bit cool for them, so they feed in the warmest water they can find.
Best water today is 8–32 ft deep, mostly on channel edges.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 50 ft, cold below.
Clear water: they bite best at dawn, dusk and on cloudy days.

species.name: Largemouth bass
why: Water 64°F on top, much colder than they like, so they move slowly and stay deep.
Best water today is 4–20 ft deep, mostly on sheltered coves.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 50 ft, cold below.
